Modern Classics: The Best of Both Worlds

Heritage sport tourers combine retro styling with modern engineering. They look like they belong in a period film but feature fuel injection, ABS, traction control, and reliable electronics underneath the classic bodywork. For riders who want the romance of a classic without the unreliability, these machines offer a compelling compromise.

Why Heritage Tourers Appeal

There is a growing movement of riders who reject the aggressive styling and complex electronics of modern motorcycles in favour of simpler, more elegant machines. Heritage tourers satisfy this desire while providing the safety, reliability, and performance that make modern touring genuinely enjoyable and safe.

Best Heritage Sport Tourers 2026

Triumph Speed Twin 1200 — The 1200cc parallel twin delivers 98bhp with a characterful exhaust note. Modern electronics including ride modes, traction control, and ABS hide beneath the gorgeous retro bodywork. Comfortable enough for multi-day tours with the right accessories. The definitive heritage tourer.

BMW R nineT — The air-cooled boxer evokes classic BMW heritage while delivering modern performance. Shaft drive, ABS, and fuel injection ensure reliability. Multiple variants from cafe racer to scrambler allow personal expression.

Kawasaki Z900RS — Retro styling inspired by the legendary Z1 with a modern 948cc inline four. Smooth, powerful, and blessed with excellent handling. The SE version adds premium Ohlins suspension for touring confidence.

Royal Enfield Continental GT 650 — The budget heritage option. The 648cc parallel twin is smooth, economical, and characterful. At under seven thousand pounds new it is remarkably affordable. Not the fastest tourer but deeply enjoyable on B-roads.

Moto Guzzi V7 Stone Special — Italian style with a transverse V-twin and shaft drive. The engine character is addictive and the low seat height gives confidence. Parts availability is good through the dedicated Guzzi community.

Making a Heritage Bike Tour-Ready

  • Luggage — Vintage-style leather or canvas panniers maintain the aesthetic. Longride, Hepco and Becker, and Legend Gear offer classic-styled bags with modern fastening systems.
  • Screen — A small fly screen adds wind protection without ruining classic lines. Dart, Puig, and National Cycle make tasteful options.
  • Comfort — Bar-end mirrors, gel seat pads, and heated grips add touring comfort without visual compromise.
  • Protection — Engine bars and frame sliders protect against tip-over damage without looking out of place on a heritage machine.
Heritage touring is about style as much as substance. Part of the pleasure is arriving at your destination on a beautiful machine that turns heads and starts conversations. These bikes make every stop a social event.

The Heritage Community

The modern classic community is one of the most welcoming in motorcycling. Clubs like the Triumph Owners MCC, BMW Boxer Club, and various cafe racer groups organise touring weekends and rallies specifically for heritage bikes. faq.q: What is a heritage sport tourer?
faq.a: A heritage sport tourer combines retro styling with modern engineering. It looks like a classic but features fuel injection, ABS, traction control, ride modes and reliable electronics beneath the period bodywork. This gives riders the romance and elegance of an older machine along with the safety, dependability and performance that make modern touring genuinely enjoyable and safe. The Triumph Speed Twin 1200 is a leading example.

faq.q: Can you tour comfortably on a heritage bike?
faq.a: Yes, with the right accessories. Most heritage bikes are comfortable enough for multi-day tours once you add vintage-style leather or canvas panniers, a small fly screen for wind protection, and comfort touches like gel seat pads and heated grips. These upgrades maintain the classic aesthetic while adding genuine touring ability. The upright riding position of many models is naturally comfortable over distance.

faq.q: Which is the best value heritage tourer?
faq.a: The Royal Enfield Continental GT 650 is the standout budget option at under seven thousand pounds new. Its 648cc parallel twin is smooth, economical and characterful, and while it is not the fastest tourer, it is deeply enjoyable on B-roads. For a step up in power and refinement, the Triumph Speed Twin 1200 and Kawasaki Z900RS offer more performance at a higher price.

faq.q: How do I make a heritage bike tour-ready?
faq.a: Add vintage-style leather or canvas panniers from brands like Longride or Legend Gear to keep the aesthetic, fit a small fly screen from Dart or Puig for wind protection, and improve comfort with bar-end mirrors, a gel seat pad and heated grips. Engine bars and frame sliders protect against tip-over damage without looking out of place. None of these compromise the classic looks.
